derivation: Generated by tools/import_kicad_board.py from the vendor's own KiCad footprint. Pad centres are exact to three decimal places in millimetres, scaled at 8.0 px/mm from a 25.24 x 20.16 mm extent including a 1.0 mm margin. Pin names joined from the symbol library on pad number. Nothing here was measured off an image.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are what tools/import_pindefs.py read out of the sources named in `pindefs`: the vendor's own CAD, `seeed-pcb`, for `NFC2`, `NFC1`, `54L15_RX20`, `54L15_TX20`, and the board-support packages for the rest; a pad whose `chip_pin` is null says why in `why_null`. No board module describes nRF54L15 here, so no level is read for any pad and the pin view reports every one as not modelled until a module and a core exist; `chip_pin` is recorded so that the join is ready, not made. 20 pins on this board are named with NO flat number -- P2.08, P1.11, P1.10, and so on -- so every pad reaching one carries `chip_index` null for that reason and not for a missing reading: no flat GPIO numbering is published for the nRF54L15 at all, so a module for it would key its own table the way webui/boards/samd21.py does, and until one exists no level is read for any pad here.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py from the sources in `packages`, at those revisions, and not every one of them is a board-support package. The vendor's own CAD among them, `seeed-pcb`, answered `NFC2`, `NFC1`, `54L15_RX20`, `54L15_TX20`; the board-support package, `zephyr`, answered every other pad that resolves. Nothing was inferred from the silkscreen or a pinout image: a label resolves only when every source in `packages` that defines it names the same pin, and `python tools/import_pindefs.py <board>` prints the file that named it. The reason given for each of `USER_LED`, `SAMD11_SWDIO`, `SAMD11_EN`, `nRF54_EN`, `nRF54_SWDIO`, `SAMD11_SWCLK`, `nRF54_SWCLK` having no `chip_pin` cites the vendor's own board CAD.

packages.name: seeed-pcb
packages.repository: https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/ -- each XIAO's own page, as a zip
packages.licence: OSHW, per Seeed's XIAO series repository

pads.label: USER_LED
pads.why_null: the board's user LED. Two sources name its pin and neither names this pad: Seeed's own nRF54L15.kicad_pcb has a net 'P2.00{slash}USR_LED' carrying the nRF54L15's own P2.00 pad, a green LED and a test point, and Zephyr's xiao_nrf54l15 board states the same pin independently as `led0 = <&gpio2 0>`. NOT written into `chip_pin`: the vendor spells this pad USER_LED in the symbol library the labels come from and USR_LED in the board file, and no file here says those are one pad

pads.label: SAMD11_SWDIO
pads.why_null: this pad reaches the on-board debugger, an ATSAMD11D14A, and not this board's own MCU; `chip_pin` names a pin of the board's MCU, so a number here would be a pin of the wrong chip. Seeed's own board file names both parts, and the debugger's pins are reachable from it if they are ever wanted under a field that says which chip it means

pads.label: SAMD11_EN
pads.why_null: this pad is named for the on-board debugger, an ATSAMD11D14A, and not for this board's own MCU; `chip_pin` names a pin of the board's MCU, so a number here would be a pin of the wrong chip. NOT claimed: which pin it reaches. No net in Seeed's own board file carries this pad's name, so unlike the SWDIO and SWCLK pads on the same header nothing here was traced

pads.label: nRF54_EN
pads.why_null: a reset pad of the nRF54L15, not a GPIO: in Seeed's own nRF54L15.kicad_pcb this pad lands on the underside test point TP4, whose net '~{nRF54_RESET}' carries the nRF54L15's own pad D2 '~{RESET}', which its footprint names apart from its pads numbered P0.00 through P2.10 by port and bit. A reset is a dedicated pin of the silicon, so there is no GPIO number for this label to have

pads.label: nRF54_SWDIO
pads.why_null: a dedicated debug pad of the nRF54L15, not a GPIO: Seeed's own nRF54L15.kicad_pcb names its thirty-two pads P0.00 through P2.10 by port and bit and names this one 'SWDIO' separately, alongside the supplies and the crystal, so there is no GPIO number for it to have
